prompt:
Image 1 is the camera and pose guide: grey clay maquettes in exactly this grid, rendered from the game's battle camera; the coloured areas on them mark where the side's cloth goes. Copy from it exactly the camera angle, the direction every figure faces, the pose in each cell, the size of the figure in its cell and the grid. Do not copy its smooth grey clay surfaces, its simple shapes or its toy-like proportions.
Image 2 is a finished sprite sheet from the same game, painted at the same camera and in the same view: match its camera angle, the size of its figures in their cells, its daylight and its painting. Do not copy its soldier, his kit, his weapon or his colours (no orange anywhere, no axe, no horns, no antlers); its grid of poses is not the one to copy (Image 1's is).
Image 3 is a painted portrait from the same game, a reference for the painting hand and for the materials only: do not paint that person, and do not copy its dark background, its candlelight or its head-and-shoulders framing.

A game sprite sheet: 16 full-length painted figures of one soldier, one figure in each cell of a 4 by 4 grid, on a perfectly flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF) background. The same soldier, the same equipment, the same colours and the same scale in every cell; only the pose changes.

Camera: high above and behind, looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at miniatures on a table; orthographic, with no perspective, so every figure is the same size. Every figure faces away from us, toward the upper right of the image: we see its back, its right side, the top of its helmet or hood and the tops of its shoulders; its face is hidden. The figures are foreshortened as seen from above: the top of the head and the shoulders are large, the legs short.

Light: outdoor daylight. A high sun in the upper left of the image lights the tops of helmets and hoods, the shoulders and the upper-left side of every figure with warm highlights; a cool blue-grey sky fill lies in the shadows on the lower-right side. No candlelight, no dramatic dark shadows, nothing glows unless the description below says so. No cast shadow on the background.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, the same hand as the painted portrait references; a muted earthy palette of charcoal, ash grey, dull iron, bark brown, leather and bone, in which the side's cloth is the one clear hue; soft painterly edges, with small crisp highlights on metal edges and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges of every figure. Each figure has a strong, simple, readable silhouette that still reads when the figure is shrunk to 40 pixels tall. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no chibi or big-headed proportions, no glossy 3D render, no pixel art.

The soldier: A Thorn Militia levy spearman: a bark-brown leather jerkin, worn under a sleeveless surcoat of deep bottle-green cloth that covers his whole chest and belly from the collar down to just below the knees, front and back, split at the front below the belt so the legs can stride and held at the waist by a knotted rope belt; a short deep bottle-green hooded cloak with the hood up, covering the shoulders and the upper back; padded sleeves and leather bracers; wrapped legs and soft boots; bark-brown weathered skin; a long dark hawthorn spear with a barbed head of bone and iron shaped like a great thorn. No shield, no antlers. Plain and poor.

Side colour: The raised hood, the short cloak and the long surcoat are the side's cloth, dyed deep bottle green: the colour of jade or of a green glass bottle held to the light, a clear and fairly saturated cool green, a little bluer than grass and much more colourful than the grey, brown and leather of the rest of the kit. These are large, clean, unbroken areas that face the sky and the camera, so that a packed block of these soldiers reads as that green from far away: about a third of what the camera sees of each standing figure is this cloth. Lighter and still clearly green where the sun strikes it, deep bottle green in its middle tones, dark green in the shade. Never leaf-green, yellow-green or olive; never grey, slate, dusty or blackish; never as blue as teal. It is painted with the same brushwork as the rest.

Facing, again: every figure in every one of the cells faces the same way, away from us toward the upper right, including the figure that is hit, the falling one and the fleeing ones; no face is seen anywhere on this sheet.

Detail: at full size each figure is a finished small painting, not a flat icon: individual bark plates with worn edges, cloth folds with frayed tips, leather straps and buckles, wood grain, a worn blade or point; varied, visible brush strokes. The values stay simple enough that the figure reads at 40 pixels: a light top (headgear, shoulders, cloth) against darker legs.

Proportions and scale: realistic adult proportions, the head with its helmet or hood about one sixth of the standing height; weapons at true size. Standing upright, a figure is about 62% of its cell's height; lying figures are as long as the standing ones are tall.

The cells, left to right, row by row (the poses of the camera and pose guide):
1. (row 1, column 1) standing ready, weight on both feet.
2. (row 1, column 2) standing at ease, weight shifted onto one leg, head turned a little to one side.
3. (row 1, column 3) marching: left foot forward in a long stride, right foot pushing off behind.
4. (row 1, column 4) marching: right foot forward in a long stride, left foot pushing off behind.
5. (row 2, column 1) attack windup: the weapon drawn far back, body twisted and coiled.
6. (row 2, column 2) the strike: the weapon fully extended into the blow, lunging forward on the front foot.
7. (row 2, column 3) follow-through: the weapon swept past the target and low, body turned with the swing.
8. (row 2, column 4) braced: the weapon held ready in both hands across the body, knees bent, leaning into the enemy.
9. (row 3, column 1) hit from the front: the soldier lurches backward toward us with his back still turned to us, shoulders hunched, arms thrown out to the sides, head bowed forward; we see only the back of his head or helmet and his back, never his face.
10. (row 3, column 2) falling backward toward us, knees buckling, about halfway to the ground; still seen from behind and above: the back of the head or helmet and the back toward us.
11. (row 3, column 3) lying dead on the ground on its back, limbs loose.
12. (row 3, column 4) lying dead on the ground face down, a different sprawl.
13. (row 4, column 1) fleeing in panic away from the enemy: running hard, weapon dropped, looking back over the shoulder.
14. (row 4, column 2) fleeing: the other foot forward, arms pumping, looking back.
15. (row 4, column 3) victory cheer: weapon raised high overhead, other fist raised, shouting.
16. (row 4, column 4) no person: only the weapon lying flat on the ground, as dropped.

Weapon motion: thrust: windup = spear drawn back at hip height, strike = a straight forward thrust, follow = the point dipping after the thrust.

Background and separation: one flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor, vignette or shadow; at least 24 pixels of clean background between any two figures and around the edges. No magenta, pink or purple anywhere on the figures.

Never: text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames, signatures, logos; a floor, ground, scenery or cast shadows; blood; extra people; cropped or overlapping figures.
